d: MEI LI is a specialty restaurant that celebrates contemporary Chinese cuisine rooted in tradition. Integrating China’s rich heritage and culture with modern elements and an experiential flair, Mei Li stands out for its approachable and engaging appeal.

As a Chef De Partie, you will be responsible to assist with the efficient running of the department in line with Hyatt International's Corporate Strategies and brand standards, whilst meeting employee, guest and owner expectations.

The Chef de Partie is responsible to supervise the assigned station / section of the outlet kitchen, in order to prepare a consistent, high quality product and ensure courteous, professional, efficient and flexible service that supports the outlet’s/function operating concept and Hyatt International standards
q: A potential candidate should ideally have
Minimum 2 years work experience as Chef de Partie or 3-4 years as Demi Chef de Partie/Commis in a hotel or large Chinese restaurant with good standards
Preferably with experience in luxury international brands. Qualification in Kitchen Production or Management will be an advantage.
Comprehensive knowledge of kitchen hygiene practices and occupational health and safety standards will be essential.
Basic Computer Skills in MS Office, and Recipe Maintenance System is preferred.

d: CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER - IRx WORKFORCE OPERATIONS
Reports to: JV Board, with four directors, two from each of IRx and Ashley Services Group Limited (ASG) an Australian publicly listed company.
Appointment: Full General Manager and P&L responsibility, with a seat on the JV Board
Package: Fixed salary, performance-related pay and equity subject to agreed vesting terms
Start: On or before 1 January 2027, to coincide with incorporation. Earlier mobilisation preferred.
Build a significant business. Transform workforce operations at scale.

IRx and Australia's Ashley Technology Pty Ltd (part of Ashley Services Group) are seeking a Chief Executive Officer to lead IRx Workforce Operations, their joint venture bringing proven workforce management technology (ATHEXIS) to Qatar, with GCC expansionto follow.
We want a leader who understands workforce-intensive businesses, has the trust of owners and executives, and can turn relationships into commercial growth.

The business is built on ATHEXIS, Ashley Technology’s cloud workforce and operations platform. It was developed from 12 years of operational use and is live with 90+ clients across logistics, retail, mining, construction, rail and defence. Organisations that have implemented ATHEXIS report a 33% cut in time-and-attendance admin and 42,890 overtime hours saved across its client base.
People: capacity planning, rostering with anti-double-allocation rules, mobile timesheets, and recruitment with AI candidate filtering.
Assets and tasks: allocation of assets and tasks alongside people, with actual vs planned hours.
Contracts: real-time costing and reporting across sites, employment agreements and jurisdictions.
Compliance: qualifications, clearances, right to work and safety workflows. Workers with expired credentials are blocked from being rostered.

Qatar is a strong fit. It has a large, mobile workforce, heavy compliance obligations (visas, labour regulation, accommodation, transport, supply-chain assurance), and an energy expansion that will drive major turnarounds. Much of this is still managed on spreadsheets.

The JV will go to market as a Qatar company on proven international technology, tailored for Qatari operations, starting with oil and gas. It combines IRx's relationships and industrial ecosystem with Ashley Technology’s operating experience and platform.
You report to the JV Board. You are accountable for strategy, commercial results, delivery, organisation, P&L and cash.
Build a focused pipeline of 10–15 priority accounts, aiming for five or six real prospects in play at any time. Sales cycles in Qatar are long, so no single deal can carry the plan.
Engage owners, CEOs and operational leaders, and lead major pursuits through to negotiation, contract signature and collection.

Work with IRx's senior executives, who open doors at CEO and C-suite level. You own the relationship day to day and drive it to close. Work with Ashley Technology on technical aspects of the product and its delivery and with IRx for business operations.
Lead with the customer's problem, not the product. Build business cases on cost visibility, compliance risk, productivity and capacity planning.
Run proof-of-concept and pilot programmes, typically 12 weeks on the customer's own historical data. Qualify prospects hard so pilots convert to paid contracts.
Shape pricing to each customer: subscription plus per-person or transactional fees, with consumption-based entry offers in year one. Price on value delivered, not cost to serve.
Expand deployments across customer sites, contracts and business units. Cross-sell the wider IRx offering with the Board's agreement.
Help customers improve deployment, utilisation, productivity, cost visibility and compliance through better workflows and realdigital adoption.
Use benchmarking, such as cost per transaction or cost per unit of work, to show customers where the value is.

Build in-country first-line support and an implementation capability. Use delivery partners (typically international Systems Integrators with whom IRx have a partnership) where it makes sense, project by project.
Work with Ashley Technology technical team on second and third-line support, on the roadmap and on Qatar-specific configuration. There is one global product, with no forks.
Meet Qatar data-residency and security requirements, with in-country hosting and a credible path through Microsoft's ecosystem.
Own deployment success, measured value, renewals and expansion.
Recruit and develop the team and manage budgets and margins. Year one aims to be cost-neutral, with Ashley Technology and IRx co-funding the early stage until revenue carries the business.
Report clearly to the Board and bring recommendations, not just updates.

Work within the Board's governance: reserved matters, dual signatories and delegated authority limits. Manage the Qatar tender mechanics, including bid and performance bonds, parent guarantees and JV capitalisation.
Use in-country value (ICV), Qatarisation and local-spend scoring as a commercial advantage in tenders.
Engage the national ecosystem, including Tawteen, QDB, QRDI and innovation funding.
Build the JV's local identity and brand with IRx and Ashley Technology.

Qatar is the focus for 2027. Build commercially justified cases for GCC expansion, through local-partner entities where required, and for integration with the wider IRx ecosystem (for example ADAPT), as agreed with the Board.
Mobilise with the JV, in post from incorporation (target 31 December 2026).
Q1 2027: agree the priority account list and launch a Qatar oil and gas–tailored sandpit.
Q1–Q2 2027: run at least three pilots or proofs of concept.
By June 2027: sign the first paying customer.
Stand up in-country hosting, support and a delivery partner model.
Draft the three-year strategic plan for Board approval.
q: Senior leadership in a workforce-intensive sector such as energy, construction, facilities, logistics, manpower or contracting. P&L ownership is essential.
A genuine Qatar network at owner, CEO and operations level, and a track record of turning it into signed contracts.
Strong understanding of Qatar business culture. Credibility and relationships matter more than any pitch.
Experience selling complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise solutions with long cycles. Technology, SaaS or digital transformation experience is a strong advantage.
A founder's mindset: able to start with a small team and a blank sheet, stay on every deal daily, and build the team around you.
Comfortable operating on site as well as in the boardroom.
Sound judgement on governance, compliance and ethics. The JV walks away from business that fails these tests.
Candidates will go through structured assessment by both Joint Venture partners.

d: Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.
The company is founder-led, profitable, and growing.

We are seeking a highly motivated and experienced IHV Alliance Sales Director to join our strategic partnerships team who will be responsible for leading IHV Alliances globally, in AMER, EMEA or APAC regions. Reporting to the Head of IHV Alliances, the IHV Alliance Sales Director will work closely with IHV and Canonical teams in those geographies to develop and maintain strong relationships with senior executives at strategic partner organizations, fostering collaboration and alignment on joint business objectives. The IHV Alliance Sales Director will manage and grow a team of Business Development Managers and help them identify and pursue new business opportunities with IHVs, driving revenue growth and market expansion, develop and execute go-to-market strategies for joint offerings, oversee the day-to-day management of alliances including contract negotiations and performance tracking, and issue resolution.

The Director is responsible for building trusted relationships with IHV partners, increasing Canonical market share and attach rate, evangelising the partnership and leading all business interactions from engineer to CxO. They will often run customer workshops focused on particular initiatives at that customer, attend sales events, give public presentations and lead executive engagements.
Location: This role will be based remotely in AMER, EMEA or APAC regions.
q: Experience in alliance or indirect sales management roles
Ability to capture customer requirements, evaluate gaps, identify and create opportunities
Passionate about Ubuntu products and mission
Comfortable in fast-paced and high pressure environments with measurable goals
Experience with Linux, virtualization, containers, and other cloud technologies.

We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognize outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits which reflect our values and ideals. Team Member Assistance Program & Wellness Platform

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open-source projects and the platform for AI, IoT, and the cloud, we are changing the world of software. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence; in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Most colleagues at Canonical have worked from home since our inception in 2004. Working here is a step into the future and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.
Canonical is an equal opportunity employer

We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.
